section_summary.extract_value: This section details the factor analysis of Romanian BAS-2 scores, focusing on the fit of a one-factor solution using Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) with a subsample of 243 participants. It describes the initial model fit indices, the subsequent modifications made to improve the model by freeing error covariances between specific items, and the acceptable fit indices of the revised one-dimensional structure, along with the Cronbach's alpha for this subsample.
section_summary.evidence_source: The results of the principal-axis factor analyses with the above subsamples point to a one-dimensional factor structure for Romanian BAS-2 scores, with all 10 items loading onto this dimension. We, therefore, examined the fit of this hypothesised one-factor solution using CFA with the second subsample (n = 243). Skewness and kurtosis were below critical limits for CFA (Kline, 2005), so no data were transformed prior to analysis. The standardised estimates of factor loadings for the best-fitting model were all very good-to-excellent (see Fig. 1). Fit indices values were found to be: 2 M(35) = 213.719, p < .001, 2 normed = 6.106, p < .001, CFI = .848, RMSEA= .142 with 90% CI = .124–.161, SRMR = .068. These results indicate that fit indices values were not found to be at acceptable intervals. Brown (2014) recommends that error covariances should be freed if there is a theoretical or measurement rationale for doing so. We, therefore, consulted modification indices to free error covariances between Items #2 and #9 due to the similar wording between these items, and between Items #4 and #7 (both items reflect positive and unique body characteristics) and Items #1 and #5 (both items represent attentiveness to the body). This one-dimensional structure provided an acceptable fit to the data: -2 M(32) = 98.029, p < .001, normed = 3.063, p < .001, CFI = .950, RMSEA= .090 (low = .070, high = .111), SRMR = .049 (see Fig. 1). Cronbach's alpha was .89 (95% CI = .87–.91) for this subsample.
